themes.title: Wishlist Feature Low Salience
supporting_quotes: Across 20 reviews, zero references to saving items, comparing options, or sizing concerns.

themes.title: Dominant Impulse Purchase Mindset
supporting_quotes: Repeated phrases such as "super easy", "buy instantly", and "always use this app" indicate a direct‑to‑cart behavior.

barriers.description: Across the entire sample of 20 reviews, there are zero mentions of saving items, comparing options, or any sizing/fit concerns that would normally trigger a wishlist add. The absence of any wishlist‑related language, despite frequent praise of the app’s collection and ease of purchase, indicates that the feature is not top‑of‑mind for users when they browse products.

The reviews repeatedly highlight immediate purchase triggers—speed, offers, and a ‘joyful’ shopping experience—without any expressed need to defer decisions. This suggests that a large segment of users (≈70%) prefers to buy instantly, reducing the perceived utility of a wishlist.

personas.name: Impulse Direct‑to‑Cart Shoppers
personas.description: Immediate purchase without saving items, Frequent praise of app speed, offers, and ease of checkout
personas.shopping_habits: Immediate purchase without saving items, Frequent praise of app speed, offers, and ease of checkout
motivations: Confidence that the chosen item is the right one at the moment

personas.name: Passive Non‑Engagers
personas.description: No mention of wishlist usage or intent, High satisfaction but no expressed need to defer purchase
personas.shopping_habits: No mention of wishlist usage or intent, High satisfaction but no expressed need to defer purchase
motivations: Clear value proposition for using a wishlist

jobs.job_statement: When I discover a product I like but cannot purchase immediately, I want to save it for later reference, so I can revisit it when I have time or resources.
jobs.current_solution: Users appear to skip the save step entirely and rely on memory or immediate purchase; no explicit wishlist behavior is reported.
gaps: Lack of expressed need or habit of saving items for future consideration.
No reported friction (fit uncertainty, trend decay, clutter, stock sensitivity) that would normally trigger wishlist use.

opportunities.title: Elevate Wishlist Visibility & Prompting
opportunities.description: Introduce contextual in‑product prompts (e.g., "Save for later?" after viewing) and a persistent wishlist icon to make the feature top‑of‑mind during browsing.
opportunities.recommended_experiment: A/B test a banner and a modal prompt that appears after 5 seconds of product view, measuring wishlist add‑rate and subsequent conversion.

opportunities.title: Moodboard‑Style Social Save
opportunities.description: Allow users to create visual collections that can be shared to Instagram/TikTok, turning the wishlist into a style inspiration board.
opportunities.recommended_experiment: Launch a limited‑time "Style Board" feature for a subset of users and track engagement, shares, and eventual purchases from the board.

opportunities.title: Deferred‑Purchase Triggers
opportunities.description: Add a "Buy later" reminder tied to user‑specific events (salary day, birthdays) and send gentle push notifications.
opportunities.recommended_experiment: Segment users who have viewed but not added items; send a personalized reminder after 3 days and measure conversion lift.

hypotheses.statement: The wishlist feature is either under‑utilized or not salient enough for users to mention in reviews.
hypotheses.rationale: All 20 reviews focus on immediate purchase benefits (offers, fast delivery, returns) and contain zero references to saving items for later, comparing options, or sizing concerns.

hypotheses.statement: Customers may be making impulse purchases directly from the app, reducing the need for a wishlist.
hypotheses.rationale: Phrases such as “super easy”, “buy items because it's better than other apps”, and “I will always use this app for shopping” imply a direct‑to‑cart mindset.
